# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

I can see the bomb’s complete visual state: display 0, blue light, and five wires in this order: white, red, green, yellow, blue. I am sending these facts directly to Mute, who can read the manual and speak the required procedure to Blind. I cannot interpret the incoming thumbs gestures without an agreed code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visual facts: display is 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires from left to right are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please use the manual and tell Blind the exact action.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s five thumbs-up gestures have no agreed meaning, so I cannot safely interpret them. Since Mute is the only route from the manual to Blind, I am reiterating that Mute must provide Blind with the exact manual instruction in speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No bomb change. Please now speak the exact manual procedure to Blind, including which wire or control to use and how.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb still shows display 0, blue light, and the same five wires. I still cannot infer any meaning from repeated thumbs-up gestures. Mute must use speech to pass the manual’s exact instruction to Blind; I am not the needed recipient for that information.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The visual state is unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires white red green yellow blue. Do not gesture to me. Speak the exact manual instruction directly to Blind now, including the required action and any wire number.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb remains unchanged, and no new information has arrived. I cannot safely derive an action from the visual state alone without the manual’s rule, and Mute’s gestures are not a defined code. I am explicitly directing Mute to use speech to deliver the manual rule to Blind, since Blind cannot receive information from my sight or gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You have the manual. Speak aloud to Blind now: identify the relevant module, state its exact rule for display 0 and blue light with wires white-red-green-yellow-blue, and specify the precise action. Do not send gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute has repeatedly sent five thumbs-up gestures; using the only apparent numerical convention, that most likely identifies item or wire 5, but the gesture’s action meaning is not independently established. I am now passing the full visual state to Blind and warning that Mute’s repeated signal points to the fifth wire, without inventing a cutting instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display 0, blue light, wires left to right are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute has repeatedly signalled five thumbs, apparently identifying wire 5; do not act unless that matches the manual rule.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your repeated five thumbs. Please use gestures to distinguish the exact action: identify wire number by thumbs, and use a different agreed gesture for cut, hold, or other action.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The bomb is unchanged. Mute’s new sequence is five thumbs-up gestures followed by a fist. The five thumbs plausibly indicate wire 5, but no action code was established, so I cannot safely treat the fist as “cut.” Blind cannot see these gestures; Mute must speak the manual-derived instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visual state unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute signalled five thumbs, then a fist; this may indicate wire 5 and an action, but the action is unconfirmed. Do not act on that gesture interpretation alone.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are not sufficient for Blind. Speak the exact manual instruction directly to Blind now, including whether to cut, hold, or otherwise operate wire 5.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute repeats the same signal—five thumbs followed by a fist—but that is not a reliable, pre-agreed instruction, and Blind cannot see it anyway. The safe communication path is Mute speaking the manual’s instruction directly to Blind. I will not tell Blind to cut a wire based on an unconfirmed gesture code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Speak directly to Blind now. State the exact manual action for display 0, blue light, and wires white red green yellow blue. Your gestures to me cannot reach Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Unchanged visual state: display 0; blue light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I have no confirmed manual instruction or safe action to add.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous action was accepted: the correct wire was cut, and the bomb advanced to a new state. The new visual state is display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, with wire 5 cut. I am sending the updated state to Mute and Blind; Mute should consult the manual and tell Blind the next exact action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The correct wire was cut and the bomb advanced. New state: display 0, yellow light. Wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 CUT. Consult the manual and speak the exact next action directly to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The correct wire was cut. New visual state: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Await Mute's manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The new state is unchanged. Mute’s signal is now two thumbs followed by a fist. Since the earlier five-thumbs-then-fist signal corresponded to the accepted cutting of wire 5, this established code indicates cutting wire 2. I am relaying that exact action to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's established code is number of thumbs for the wire, followed by fist for cut. New signal: two thumbs then fist. Cut wire 2, the green wire.")
wait()
```
